data.hypothesis: For small active grids, the original serial path avoids OpenMP startup. For larger work, a one-thread budget uses a region per timestep to expose its six-region overhead against the serial baseline, while larger budgets keep one team across all timesteps to limit startup cost and test static row-level scaling. The output math and boundary writes remain unchanged; the controller must measure and verify both paths.
data.notes: The dispatch compares region strategies across the official thread budgets rather than as a same-budget A/B, so interpret timing accordingly. Row loops use static scheduling, and the persistent loop has an implicit worksharing barrier at each timestep before buffers swap. No tests or measurements were run here; controller validation should cover smaller sizes and n=256. The only measured program currently available is the correct serial baseline (baseline-e1, mean 0.4575 s); the catalog has no candidate comparisons yet.
transformations: Preserved the serial stencil and output initialization; route small active workloads through the serial implementation.
Added a shared row kernel and static OpenMP work sharing over collapsed z/y row loops.
Use a separate parallel region per timestep for larger one-thread calls and a persistent team across all six timesteps for multi-thread calls, with num_threads set from the call budget.
